prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1218; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured's vehicle was sideswiped while changing lanes. The claimant reports a neck strain and says the other vehicle drifted into the lane as they moved over.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the collision the same way as in the first report. The account has stayed consistent across every conversation so far.

Entry 4: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. Independent witnesses describe the sideswipe as it was reported to us.

Entry 5: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement both match the described impact. Damage to the vehicle is mostly consistent with a side-to-side contact of this kind.

Entry 6: Checked prior claims and records for the vehicle and found no earlier damage on file. The claimant has also reported no earlier problems with the neck or upper back.

Entry 7: The reported neck strain is a plausible injury for a lateral impact of this type. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so the file will be reviewed at the next interval.

Entry 8: Medical records and treatment notes are being gathered to support the injury timeline. Claim remains open pending the final medical update and repair estimate review.
